admitted.text: Randi seems terrified that Pace’s tenderness can reach the self beneath her polished performance.
admitted.detail_quote: He could have the face. The face was very good. The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Randi reads as fiercely controlled, using beauty and social fluency to keep her vulnerable self hidden.
admitted.detail_quote: Kentucky, until she was nine — one more of the things she let him see that nobody else did. It came out of hiding when something moved her.

admitted.text: After being seen she seems to turn on herself with a small, secret act of self-hurt.
admitted.detail_quote: set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed — slow and steady, down into the nail bed, where it would hurt.

admitted.text: She seems to cover her own desire for women by passing it off as a gift to her boyfriend.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable

admitted.text: Randi reads as genuinely hungry for Vee before she can make that desire socially safe.
admitted.detail_quote: Yes, she said. The word came out alone, with nothing around it

admitted.text: Randi seems genuinely softened by Vee, with an unperformed tenderness escaping her usual management.
admitted.detail_quote: the esses running long, the a's lifting, more of whatever it was than there had been when they sat down

admitted.text: Randi seems sincerely tender toward Vee even while deliberately drawing out Vee’s secrets.
admitted.detail_quote: Then he's right in front of you. On his knees. Looking up. And what did he *see*?

admitted.text: Randi reads as skilled at making invasiveness feel like permission and shame feel like intimacy.
admitted.detail_quote: They don't, sweetheart. You can't get a true line through an inch of padding.

admitted.text: She seems to want to be Vee's first woman almost possessively, as something that would last.
admitted.detail_quote: She'll be eighty years old and she'll remember the first one.

admitted.text: Randi reads as increasingly jealous of Pace’s unhurried access to Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: the side of her bent forefinger went to her teeth and she bit down on the knuckle, briefly, and took it away

admitted.text: Dropping "tell me" seems to signal that their shared fantasy has turned painful for her.
admitted.detail_quote: Every night in this house she had said it, at his ear, against his mouth

admitted.text: Her strict control over food seems to stand for a larger habit of denying herself.
admitted.detail_quote: not even a glance back at the tray

admitted.text: Pace seems tender in ways that are practical, anticipatory, and nearly invisible.
admitted.detail_quote: He had sliced it thin because she would eat thin slices and would not eat thick ones

admitted.text: His insistence on consent seems sincere and principled.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: His restraint seems to be shaped by an old failure with a woman named Daphne.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: Daphne reads as the unseen source of Pace’s hard-won respect for emotional privacy.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: He seems to protect what Vee confides in him even from Randi, which reads as integrity.
admitted.detail_quote: It was not his to hand across.

admitted.text: Pace reads as accepting secrecy once he can imagine it as the wrapping around a gift.
admitted.detail_quote: And she would not know, until she did.

admitted.text: Pace reads as aroused by directing another person toward a self she has not yet admitted.
admitted.detail_quote: He wanted to be in the room. He wanted to be the reason she was in the room.

admitted.text: He seems blind to what Randi feels, reading her hurt as nothing more than desire.
admitted.detail_quote: It was the want, he thought, with an edge on it tonight, from somewhere.

admitted.text: He seems quietly wounded by Randi's growing distance.
admitted.detail_quote: something in his chest he had not been ready for, low and plain, that she had not wanted to stay.

admitted.text: She reads as hungry for belonging, dazzled by people who seem to be at the center of things.
admitted.detail_quote: she had been chosen, plainly, for reasons she didn't need to understand, by exactly the person she'd have chosen to be chosen by.

admitted.text: Vee reads as accustomed to monitoring her body through her mother’s punitive vocabulary.
admitted.detail_quote: The voice said *floozie* in her mother's exact word and her thighs pressed once, hard, on their own, under her jeans.

admitted.text: Vee reads as discovering that shame and desire run together in her rather than canceling each other.
admitted.detail_quote: there was no seam, they ran on the same wire, and she had stopped looking for one.

admitted.text: She seems to feel an attraction to Randi that she will not let herself name.
admitted.detail_quote: the heat the picture put low in Vee was a heat she had no shelf for and would have died before naming at this table.

admitted.text: She seems ready to read Randi's pain in the kindest way, which reads as trusting to the point of naivety.
admitted.detail_quote: It's a French thing, she does the kiss-kiss, she's been everywhere, that's all it is, that's just how women like her say goodbye.

admitted.text: She is starting to keep the intimate parts of her life from Cassie, which hints at a drift between them.
admitted.detail_quote: What she kept was the middle.

admitted.text: Money anxiety seems to run quietly under every outing with Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: the one thing she would not do at this table was let Randi buy her seat at it.

admitted.text: She seems to be claiming her desire as her own for the first time.
admitted.detail_quote: And I took it. For once.

admitted.text: By the end she seems to be owning being looked at rather than enduring it.
admitted.detail_quote: she stood in the middle of the light and let them look. It just felt like what she was for.

admitted.text: Vee's appetite reads as something larger than food, awakened when needing and receiving carry no judgment.
admitted.detail_quote: the plain animal rightness of needing something and being handed it.

admitted.text: Vee reads as profoundly happy with Pace while remaining unaware that her happiness has been cultivated inside an older shared plan.
admitted.detail_quote: She had not been keeping the words. She had been keeping the feeling.

admitted.text: She reads as fiercely loyal, protecting Vee quietly rather than for show.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie could have pitched it up into the bleachers; she had the lungs

admitted.text: She seems to be hiding her own hurt at being left out.
admitted.detail_quote: for half a second something crossed her face and was gone before it found a name.

admitted.text: Cassie reads as the friend who sees Vee plainly without demanding that Vee perform her feelings.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie never asked — asking was for people who wanted the sad version to get bigger.

admitted.text: She reads as a warm-voiced watcher who gathers information about Randi and ranks people while she does it.
admitted.detail_quote: The not-standing was the move; Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: Her friendliness seems empty and strategic, ready to serve whatever the room needs.
admitted.detail_quote: the laugh that meant nothing on its own and was therefore available for anything.

admitted.text: She reads as the calm skeptic among Vee's friends, gently doubting that Pace is really different.
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start. I said it about Danny.

admitted.text: She reads as an eager, enthusiastic audience who gets swept up in Vee's romance.
admitted.detail_quote: We're doing hair Saturday. I'm coming to your room. This is happening.

admitted.text: The bench hidden inside a table: a hidden purpose under ordinary surfaces, waiting for Vee as well.
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The lock and key: Randi closing herself away.
admitted.detail_quote: Not tonight — and this arrived without words, quiet as a deadbolt going over — not ever.

admitted.text: The thin apple slices: rationed appetite, and Pace as the one who feeds it.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The mirror smile: a public face laid over a private self.
admitted.detail_quote: The face in the mirror was the face of a woman who had just had an extraordinary evening with her boyfriend and was about to go back out and tell him so. The face was lying.

admitted.text: The Chi Latte sign: belonging as a joke Vee has finally been let in on.
admitted.detail_quote: She had stood outside this exact joke.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: care given quietly, which Vee then keeps and wears.
admitted.detail_quote: He drew it out from under the rest and held it out to her and didn't say anything.

admitted.text: Error-correcting codes: meaning that survives noise, much as these characters talk in hints.
admitted.detail_quote: Say it more than once so the noise can't kill it.

admitted.text: The burgundy silk: being seen and fitted as herself rather than to an ideal.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't matched the dress she'd described. He'd matched *her*.

admitted.text: The riser: Vee put on display, a pedestal for being seen.
admitted.detail_quote: She crossed to it barefoot and stepped up, and the step raised her bare top into the full reach of the afternoon light

admitted.text: Randi's white-gold band: one fixed, private attachment under her changing surfaces.
admitted.detail_quote: the one fixed thing in a wardrobe that changed itself daily.

admitted.text: The folded green panties: evidence of shame converted into a deliberately offered erotic token.
admitted.detail_quote: the deep green of them particular and chosen, and the spot exactly where she'd put it.

admitted.text: Randi's uneaten bowl: refusing to be fed, a sign of the hurt between her and Pace.
admitted.detail_quote: the sauce gone to a skin over the peas and the carrot, the one line she had drawn through it still there.

admitted.text: The dress in the window: Vee's new self, carrying a hint of secrecy.
admitted.detail_quote: the dress going dark in its window at the far end of the house, getting away with something.

admitted.text: The burgundy dress: being precisely known made tangible, with Vee's desired self sewn into it.
admitted.detail_quote: This one had been cut to the actual shape of her, and to no one else's.

admitted.text: The pointing game: reads as a playful surface laid over the couple’s covert selection of another person.
admitted.detail_quote: He was not choosing a woman. He was watching her learn that she could.

admitted.text: Submersion: a refuge where Vee can be capable, weightless, and unwatched.
admitted.detail_quote: Nobody up there could see her. Nobody down here wanted anything.

admitted.text: How, and when, will Vee learn that Pace and Randi chose her together?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi and I have been together since August. We talked about you before you knew either of us.

admitted.text: How will Vee judge the freedom of her choices once she knows how carefully Randi and Pace cultivated them?
admitted.detail_quote: And she would not know, until she did.

admitted.text: Will Vee want what Randi and Pace have planned for her?
admitted.detail_quote: Yes," she said. The word came out alone, with nothing around it — the bare arrival of a thing already true before she got to it.

admitted.text: Can Randi bear Pace and Vee’s growing intimacy without turning her hunger into rivalry?
admitted.detail_quote: The words came back at him flat, with nothing on them, and he had never heard her voice do that.

admitted.text: When will Vee recognize her attraction to Randi as desire rather than glamorous friendship?
admitted.detail_quote: Randi's mouth eased back without leaving hers, and then she took a little more before she let her go.

admitted.text: What happened between Pace and Daphne, and what did it cost him?
admitted.detail_quote: it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost.

admitted.text: What caused the large scar high on Pace’s inner thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: the same uneven pink from his ribs down over his hip, a match for the one by his ear.

admitted.text: What is Pace withholding about his parents?
admitted.detail_quote: Something crossed him at *parents* — a small closing, there and gone

admitted.text: Is Brooke watching Randi, and does the sorority suspect what she is hiding?
admitted.detail_quote: a whole bright week with its own private life that Vee was no part of

admitted.text: Is Vee's friendship with Cassie being lost to Randi's world?
admitted.detail_quote: the word for a longer parting than a Wednesday

admitted.text: Will Randi keep her vow never to let Pace see her real self again?
admitted.detail_quote: Not tonight — and this arrived without words, quiet as a deadbolt going over — not ever.
